decisive_items: When she smiles, the right lower lip deviates inward; frowning, forehead wrinkling, eye closure, and nasolabial fold depth are symmetric on both sides.
the right lower lip deviates inward, whereas the rest of facial movement is symmetric
response.rationale: Isolated congenital lower lip deviation with otherwise symmetric facial movement and normal neurodevelopment/imaging is characteristic of congenital unilateral lower lip palsy. Moebius syndrome is excluded because eye closure, frowning, forehead movement, and hearing pathways are intact.

rejected.why: Moebius syndrome requires congenital facial diplegia or additional cranial nerve involvement, typically with impaired eye abduction, none of which are present; symmetric eye closure and forehead movement contradict it.
